title: Quantification of Gastric Electrical Stimulation Effects on Blood Hormones
author: Terry Powley
materials: Animals were transferred to wire hanging cages the day before surgery and then fasted for 18 h with free access to water. Rats were then anesthetized with Isoflurane Akorn Inc Catalog #NDC: 59399-106-01 (5%) in an induction box and transferred to a Somnosuite Low-flow Anesthesia System (Anesthesia system, Kent Scientific, SomnoSuite, https://www.kentscientific.com/products/somnosuite/ ) on a surgery platform SurgiSuite Multifunction Surgery Platform (Surgery platform, Kent Scientific, SurgiSuite, https://www.kentscientific.com/products/surgisuite/ ) A servo-controlled homoeothermic heating blanket, equipped with a rectal thermometer, was used to maintain body temperature at 36 °C. The level of anesthesia was reduced to 2.5% isoflurane for the surgical procedure.

See steps 6-21 of the following protocol: SPARC - Preparation of Plasma Samples from Rats by J Paul Robinson The rest of the hormone analysis process is captured in four other protocols: SPARC - Millipore Metabolic Rat Multiplex Bead Assay for Flow Cytometry SPARC - Attune NxT Set-up for Milli-metabolic bead assay Acquisition SPARC - Setting up the BEADS for the Millipore Metabolic Rat Milliplex Assay SPARC - Analysis of multiplexed bead data using MPLEX software

steps.title: Prepare Femoral Artery Catheter
steps.instruction: Establish arterial access for blood sampling in the supine rat.

substeps.instruction: Make a 1.0-1.5cm incision at the angle of the left hind leg.
Expose and separate the left femoral artery from connective tissue and femoral vein using blunt dissection.
Make a pre-cut 45 degree angle incision in the femoral wall using micro-dissecting scissors.
Insert a catheter (CX-80002S, www.BASinc.com) 2-3 cm into the artery.
Pre-fill the catheter with heparined saline (Heparin: Meitheal Pharmaceuticals Inc., 10units/ml).
Secure the catheter with sutures and connect it to the Culex automated blood sample system.

steps.title: Implant Electrodes and Strain Gauge
steps.instruction: Perform midline laparotomy and implant monitoring/stimulation devices.

substeps.instruction: Exteriorize the stomach and 3-4cm of proximal duodenum onto saline-soaked gauze pads.
Suture one or two custom-made stimulation patch electrodes (Microprobes for Life Science) onto the serosal surface of the stomach.

Glue a custom-made strain gauge (4x3.5mm, Clunbury Scientific LLC, consisting of two EA-06-031CE-350 elements) to the serosal surface of the proximal duodenum (5-15mm distal to pyloric sphincter) using Vetbond (3M corporation Catalog #1469SB), orienting it parallel to the longitudinal or circular muscle.
Exteriorize fine wire leads and connect them to a DC bridge amplifier and stimulator.

steps.title: Maintain Animal Stability
steps.instruction: Maintain the animal in a stable state post-surgery.

substeps.instruction: Keep the animal in a supine position with the abdominal area covered by saline-soaked gauze pads.
Inject normal saline continuously i.p. at 2.0ml/hr using a syringe pump.
Cover the animal with a blanket to maintain body temperature.
Reduce and maintain anesthesia at 1.5% isoflurane for the remainder of the experiment.

steps.title: Perform Blood Sampling and Stimulation
steps.instruction: Execute the stimulation protocol and collect blood samples at specified intervals.

substeps.instruction: Wait approximately one hour after surgery for the animal to stabilize.
Withdraw blood samples (0.15ml each) at the following times relative to the start of stimulation: -30 min, -5 min, 5 min, 15 min, and 30 min.
Provide electrical stimulation using a PlexStim stimulator with the following parameters: biphasic, I = 0.3mA, pw = 0.2ms, 10 Hz, 20s-on-40s-off, for 5 one-minute cycles.

steps.title: Euthanize and Perfuse Animal
steps.instruction: Terminate the animal and fix the stomach tissue.

substeps.instruction: Administer a lethal dose of Ketamine (Patterson Veterinary Catalog #07-803-6637) and Xylazine (Akorn Inc Catalog #NDC: 59399-110-20) i.p. (275mg/kg ketamine and 27.5 mg/kg xylazine).
Mark electrode locations with blue suture thread before removal.
Inspect stomach for normal distension; if required, slowly infuse warmed physiological saline (3.3ml/100g rat weight) via gavage catheter.
Transcardially perfuse the vasculature with physiological saline, followed by 4% paraformaldehyde in 0.1 mol/liter PBS (pH 7.4).

steps.title: Dissect and Map Stomach
steps.instruction: Isolate the stomach and document electrode placement.

substeps.instruction: Transect the distal esophagus and proximal duodenum, then free and remove the stomach.
Open the organ with a longitudinal cut along the greater curvature.
Separate the ventral and dorsal stomach walls via an incision along the lesser curvature to create two whole mounts.
Place the ventral half stomach in PBS in a dissecting dish under a stereomicroscope, inner surface facing up.
Mark electrode ends with pins and take a photograph of the entire surface.

Print the image at consistent magnification and measure x and y locations of the electrode midpoint relative to the pylorus end (x) and the bottom edge at the greater curvature (y) as percentage measurements.
Measure the electrode orientation relative to a line from the top of the limiting ridge (near the LES) to the bottom point near the greater curvature where the limiting ridge changes direction.
